title: The way I full on sobbed in a theater full of 3000 people while watch...
transcript: Hi, I'm Ben, and today I saw a screening of the movie Coco at the United Palace Theater in Washington Heights. The screening was hosted by Lin Manuel Miranda and featured a talk back with Miranda as well as songwriters Bobby and Kristen Anderson Lopez. I had never been to the United Palace Theater before, and I don't know if the video does it justice, but it's an absolutely gorgeous theater. The design work and detail work on the ceiling and the walls, it's just absolutely all inspiring to look at. Coco is one of my favorite Pixar movies, so I've seen it many times. But seeing it in a large theater like this with 3,000 people on a ginormous screen, which is a completely different experience. After the movie was over, Lynn came out and introduced a surprise musical performance from Mandy Gonzalez. She did a cover of Remember Me from the film, and it was absolutely incredible. After she was done, they brought out Kristen and Bobby, who spoke with Lynn for about 30 minutes. They talked a lot about kind of how they got involved in the project and what some of their inspirations were for writing remember me, given that the three of them are all songwriters. They talked a lot about the process of what it's like writing a song, specifically writing a song for Disney, and also, like, what it's like to have your song be sung by every child across the planet. Because obviously, Miranda wrote we don't talk about Bruno, Kristen and Bobby wrote let it go, and so they talked about what it was like to have a song that has that kind of cultural significance. Overall, it was a really cool event. I'm really glad I finally got to see a movie at the United Palace, and being able to hear from the songwriters and Lin after was just the cherry on top.
